content.comment_body: Hello team, I'm facing a challenge with controlling a proportional valve using a voltage range of -10V to 10V. My available module, the [product_name] AM2 AQ, provides outputs from 0 to 10V. I'm wondering if it's possible to use two outputs simultaneously—one for 0 to 10V and another for 0 to -10V, possibly with different wiring. I also have a potentiometer that ranges from -500 to 500. Is it feasible to create a program using [product_name] with AI1 translating 0 to 500 into 0 to 10V, and 0 to -500 into 0 to -10V? I've searched for solutions but haven't found any. Thanks in advance and happy holidays :) Sincerely, [user_name]
With [product_name], it is not possible to output negative voltages. Only positive output from 0 to 10V can be achieved. The system cannot generate outputs from 0 to -10V.

Thank you for the quick response! That's why I was considering if I could connect AQ1 as V1=10V & M1=0V, and AQ2 as V2=0V & M2=10V. Alternatively, is there a way to accomplish this using [product_name]—perhaps with two relays as inputs, similar to an H-bridge configuration? I believe there must be some solution for this scenario. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to control a proportional valve using a voltage output from a [company_name] module, aiming for a range of -10V to 10V. The challenge is that [product_name] output modules only support positive voltages (0-10V). The user explores possible hardware or programming alternatives but has been informed that negative analog output is unsupported. This clearly illustrates a product limitation that may not be highlighted in existing documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that [product_name] should be capable of both positive and negative analog voltage outputs, or at least provide an easy configuration method or documented workaround to achieve this.
